text:
olivia: thinking aloud — we should run a short experiment for proactive capacity tiling + per-tenant isolation. goal: reduce noisy-neighbor p99 latency spikes without over-reserving for each customer. want to capture policy shape and launch criteria.

devin: +1. can you sketch what "tiling" means here? is it time-windowed reservations or slot-based?

olivia: slot-based mostly. allocate small tiled buckets (e.g., 10s/slot) that tenants can draw burst tokens from. combine with a predictive top-up when telemetry shows rising trend for 30s.

srini: sounds doable. rough numbers from recent traffic: median slot utilization 0.12, 95th 0.6, spikes 0.9. if we make tile=10s and bucket=3 slots per tenant by default, should cover typical short bursts. we need to throttle hard at 4 slots to avoid headroom exhaustion.

maria: customers asking for guaranteed short bursts for warm startups — this could be the deliverable for the next pilot. what launch criteria do we want? my draft: 1) 3 safety customers signed for pilot, 2) <10% additional reserved GPU overhead, 3) p99 tail improvement >= 20% for pilot tenants, 4) eviction events documented and <1 per 10k reqs.

ben: agree on criteria. prioritize customers who value latency not just throughput. can we make tenant config editable via console?

olivia: yes, Console toggle + per-tenant policy fields. default auto-mode uses predictive top-up. manual override to set min-slots and max-slots.

alex: infra note — need to be careful with preemption. if we allow soft-eviction of tiles, we might cascade to other pools. recommend an isolation fence in the scheduler for tiles and a spillover policy to fallback pool with strict rate limits.

srini: +1. fallback path: route to a cheaper model variant or lower context-length worker. fallback should be explicit in policy:
```json
{
  "policy": "tile",
  "tile_duration_s": 10,
  "min_slots": 1,
  "default_slots": 3,
  "max_slots": 4,
  "predictive_topup_window_s": 30,
  "fallback": {
    "type": "variant",
    "variant_id": "low-cpu-quantized",
    "rate_limit_qps": 50
  }
}
```

devin: how do we measure correctness for predictive top-up? A couple ideas: precision of top-up (true positives where extra slots used), and false positives (allocated but unused). SRini, can you add telemetry metrics?

srini: i'll add metrics: tile_alloc_count, tile_topup_trigger_count, tile_topup_success_rate, tile_eviction_count, downstream_fallback_count. also expose latency buckets per-tenant for before/after.

maria: runbook item: when eviction_rate > 0.5% and fallback_count > X -> auto-roll back predictive top-up for that tenant and open an SRE ticket.

olivia: proposal for experiment rollout: stage-0: internal canary (team apps), stage-1: 2 pilot customers (low risk + high-value), stage-2: broader opt-in. API flag: `enable_tiled_bursting` per-tenant.

ben: timeline?

olivia: target 3-week build, 2-week internal canary, 4-week pilot. total ~9 weeks to opt-in GA gating on my launch criteria.

alex: one more infra ask — ensure we surface per-pool headroom metrics in Console (heatmap) before pilot starts. i won't sign off without that.

olivia: noted. action items: (1) srini add telemetry + dashboards (due EOW) (2) alex add isolation fence + fallback implementation plan (due 1w) (3) dev: console toggle + per-tenant fields (due 1.5w) (4) maria coordinate pilot customers (due 2w).

opsbot: deploybot: scheduled job created for feature-branch `feature/tiled-burst` — build 0.3.2 (CI started) :gear:

devin: awesome. i'll draft a short spec doc and link in product-initiative board.

maria: tagging @ben for prioritization FYI. :eyes:

olivia: thanks all — will post a spec link once devin has draft.
